name: Trap Bar Deadlift
description: The trap bar deadlift is performed inside a hexagonal barbell, gripping handles at the sides with a neutral grip. Standing inside the bar shifts the center of mass closer to the body compared to a conventional deadlift, reducing the moment arm at the hip and lumbar spine while increasing the moment arm at the knee. The result is a more quad-dominant pattern than a conventional deadlift, with less spinal stress — making it an effective compound exercise for general strength and power development.

execution.starting_position: Stand inside the trap bar with feet hip-width apart and the handles beside your hips. Push the hips back and bend the knees to grip the handles.
execution.setup_instructions: Load the bar with appropriate weight. The high handles on most trap bars reduce the range of motion — use the low handles for a full range similar to a conventional deadlift. Neutral grip is automatic with the trap bar.
steps: Step 1: Stand inside the bar, feet hip-width. Push the hips back and bend the knees until the hands reach the handles. Take a neutral grip.
Step 2: Brace the core, take a deep breath, and pull the bar tight against the floor before beginning the lift.
Step 3: Push the floor away — the leg drive is prominent with the trap bar. Drive through the full foot.
Step 4: Extend the hips and knees simultaneously to reach a fully upright position with hips locked out.
Step 5: Return the bar to the floor under control, maintaining spinal position throughout.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before the pull. Hold through the lift. Exhale at the top.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips rise faster than the shoulders — turning it into a stiff-leg pull from the lower back
Rounding the lower back due to setting up with hips too high or too low
Not using the full foot — think of leg-pressing the floor rather than just pulling with the back
safety_considerations: Easier to learn than conventional deadlift — good entry point for beginners
Still requires proper bracing — do not lift with a relaxed core
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at the top. Full setup position at the bottom with spine neutral and hips loaded.
coaching_cues: Push the floor away, not pull the bar up
Squeeze the glutes at the top to lock out
